newsitem.title: GERMANY: Norilsk strike fears may be exaggerated - Dresdner.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk strike fears may be exaggerated - Dresdner.

text.p: Expectations of a strike at Russia's Norilsk mining and metallurgical complex on March 15 may be exaggerated, Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said in a weekly precious metals report on Friday.
"...looming labour unrest in this sensitive industry in the past was usually prevented via successful negotiations," the bank said.

Platinum jumped to more than $406 per ounce at one stage on Friday, fuelled by recent news about the possibility of a strike at Norilsk next month and by delays to the opening of Russia's supply talks with Japan.
Later platinum settled back to $388/$389, still up $2.
Dresdner said Russia export agency comments had not ruled out the possibility of white metals exports resuming as early as March.
In gold, it said, central bank sales no longer looked likely for now and producers were holding back.
Dresdner saw gold underpinned at $352.50 an ounce, pegging upside potential at $370.
The London morning fix on Friday was $360.60.
